key_insight: Photodegradation in both spin-coated and gravure-printed organic solar cells is best explained by the mobility-lifetime product (μτ), not by lifetime alone.
engineering_relevance: μτ provides a practical, process-agnostic metric for predicting stability and guiding scalable organic solar cell design and printing optimization.
method: Compared spin-coated and fully roll-to-roll-compatible gravure-printed PM6:Y12 solar cells.
Tracked performance during ~1000 h of continuous illumination.
Related degradation in efficiency, mobility, lifetime, recombination, and morphology to photostability.
evidence_signal: Across both device types, power-conversion efficiency loss systematically followed μτ, while printed devices showed higher recombination lifetime but lower mobility and additional non-radiative Voc loss.
watch_item: Longer recombination lifetime does not necessarily mean better device performance, especially when mobility drops and metastable effects appear in printed architectures.
paper_title: Mobility-lifetime relation links photodegradation in spin-coated and gravure-printed organic solar cells
